compare_blocks.title: The key difference

compare_blocks.body:
The table assumes aligned conditions: the same moulded batch, the same record sheet, the same revision of the procedure, the same reviewer, the same mandatory requirements. If one is the inspector on shift and the other is only covering, duty will swamp both columns; if one has just had a record returned, behaviour will shift toward the stricter side too.

Both types can use both approaches below; the rows only state which kind of evidence tends to be taken first, and mark which axis each row sits on. This describes emphasis, not a scale of ability, and it must not be turned around into a typing table.

| The same situation | INFP: evidence likely to be attended to first | ISTJ: evidence likely to be attended to first | What this row illustrates |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A blank record sheet arrives | Keep several ways to organise the work open within the same required form | Agree on a provisional order for completing the same required fields | Outward stance, leaning J/P |
| Two parts near the upper bound, one out of tolerance | What patterns connect the measurements to the same documented process conditions | Measured values, gauge numbers and measuring times, each in its place | What counts as material, leaning S/N |
| The anomaly turns out to come from the previous process | Weigh how the required, verified details affect the people involved and make the context clear | Apply the same reporting criteria to the verified process and batch details | Standard of judgement, leaning T/F |

compare_blocks.title: One-minute comparison

compare_blocks.body:
In a fictional inspection meeting, either colleague might listen quietly or speak at length. Role, familiarity and the meeting format can all shape who speaks. Quietness does not tell you which person is more dependable.

At the letter level, both share Introversion. At the level of type dynamics, both stacks contain Fi, Ne, Si and Te. Neither similarity tells you whether the two people would look alike at work.

The difference runs along three preferences: in material, ISTJ more often trusts specific fact and experience, INFP more often trusts connection and possibility; in judgement, ISTJ more often gives the consistently applicable standard the main seat, INFP more often weighs people and values more heavily; in outer arrangement, ISTJ more often wants it settled, INFP more often wants to leave it open. The three axes have to be discussed separately — mixed together they become a personality verdict.

### INFP and ISTJ: the same inspection record, different attention

In a fictional quality review, three molded parts are sampled. Two are near the upper tolerance limit, and one is outside it. Both reviewers have the same measurements, gauge identifiers, procedure and reporting requirements.

Either reviewer must complete the required fields using the same procedure. When deciding how to explain the verified finding, both can weigh consistent reporting criteria and the risk of unfairly attributing responsibility. Those are possible T/F considerations. The order of filling in the form does not illustrate T/F or J/P.

Both emphases have a cost, and neither belongs to one type. Formatting alone can produce a complete record that cannot be read for the conditions at the time; writing the background at length can get the record returned on a mandatory field. How much that costs depends on who reads the record and what it is for.

In the fictional review, the report records the measured values, time and gauge identifier. The notes add that this was the first sample after a tooling change and that the next team was notified. The reviewer records the tooling change as a possible explanation that still needs verification.

The use of each kind of information needs stating. The traceability chain answers three things: who measured it, which revision of the procedure was used, and whether the downstream process was notified. It cannot establish that the anomaly came from the tooling change rather than equipment drift; verifying the cause means looking at equipment checks and process-parameter records, judged by whoever holds that responsibility. Neat handwriting and page count are not traceability evidence either — they are writing habits.

### INFP and ISTJ: why the four names match while the seating shifts two places

In the four-function notation used here, INFP is Fi–Ne–Si–Te and ISTJ is Si–Te–Fi–Ne. All four names are present and the order rotates by two seats: INFP's dominant Fi is third in ISTJ, and INFP's inferior Te is auxiliary in ISTJ; conversely, ISTJ's dominant Si is third in INFP, and ISTJ's inferior Ne is auxiliary in INFP.

The stacks share the judging pair Fi and Te and the perceiving pair Si and Ne. INFP leads with Fi, a judging process. ISTJ leads with Si, a perceiving process. The position in either stack says nothing about expertise or the order of steps in a real task.

Whether the third process is labelled introverted or extraverted is not uniform: for INFP's Si and ISTJ's Fi, some sources give an explicit attitude and others only the function name. When a different version turns up, check whether it names its source and read the pair through the first two positions; the disagreement does not change dominant and auxiliary. Base descriptions sit on the [INFP profile](/en/personality/infp) and the [ISTJ profile](/en/personality/istj).
compare_blocks.title: Why they are easily confused

compare_blocks.body:
Boundary of use: the three scenes below are fictional and involve only record keeping, communication and agreeing a division of work. They do not involve quality verdicts, equipment disposition or safety procedures. Anything touching a verdict or disposition follows company procedure and the person holding that responsibility.

A team can agree on what to document and how much context a later reader will need. Either colleague can spot a missing field or an incomplete explanation.

### INFP and ISTJ: before a factory audit, how the data chain and the explanatory page get split

(Fictional scene) A client is coming to audit and wants three months of records traced. The division follows who normally handles the records, who followed those two anomalies, and who knows the procedure revisions — not type. A common arrangement: whoever knows the logbooks builds the three months of sheets into one chain by batch and by procedure revision; whoever was on site writes a page explaining how the two anomalies were found, who was told and what changed afterwards.

Places missing a signature are marked and handled under the applicable records procedure. Where late signing is permitted, the actual signer, date and reason are kept — no back-dating, no signing for someone else; items that cannot be verified are left as they are rather than filled in to look tidy.

Two constraints apply. The explanatory page cannot replace the record: however detailed it is, a missing signature page is still a missing item. Nor can the chain replace the explanation: however complete, it cannot say why those two variations happened — the cause has to be verified separately.

In this fictional audit, the team samples three entries and checks who measured each part, which procedure applied and whether the next team was notified. This checks traceability in those entries. A qualified reviewer would investigate the causes separately using the relevant evidence.

### INFP and ISTJ: a cleaning rota in a shared flat

(Fictional scene) Two people share a flat and the living room and kitchen are never cleaned unless someone asks. One proposes a rota: who takes the rubbish out on which day, who mops at the weekend, tick when done. The other hesitates — will a rota turn the flatmate relationship into mutual assessment, with every missed turn recorded.

This is not about who is cleaner, and not a division by type. The one proposing worries that the work will always fall to the same person; the one hesitating worries that a table will fix things in writing and make living together harder later. Both concerns are legitimate.

A workable version splits the table into two columns: what must be done, and what gets done when noticed — only the first gets ticked. One counterexample: the proposer will also cover a flatmate's week during overtime without mentioning it, and the hesitant one will, after two weeks of putting up with it, stick the table on the fridge.

Agree a checkpoint: look at the table together on the last weekend of each month, adjust the division only, do not reopen old grievances. If someone genuinely stops doing their part over a long period, talk to them separately rather than reworking the whole table.

### INFP and ISTJ: the record comes back from review

(Fictional scene) The review comment comes back as "remarks too general". The first thing to do has nothing to do with type: establish whether the comment means the facts were unclear, that mandatory fields were missing, or both. Different targets, different fixes.

If the facts were unclear, what gets added is the process at the time: when it was discovered, which values it rested on, who was notified, how it was handled afterwards. If fields were missing, what gets added is the mandatory cells, units, signatures and dates. If both, list what is missing against the comment first, then decide what can be fixed on the spot and what needs verification back on site.

Responding to the same comment, the two may work differently: one more often compares clause by clause against the procedure to confirm the revised version passes the same requirements; the other more often restates the situation first to confirm that a reader will not misread where responsibility lies. Both work; who checks the revision afterwards follows duty, not type.
compare_blocks.title: Illustrative scenarios

compare_blocks.body:
INFP does not indicate rule-breaking. A person of either type can know the procedure thoroughly and object to a record that omits facts or unfairly assigns blame.

ISTJ does not indicate indifference. A person of either type may insist on measured values because clear records protect coworkers as well as product quality.

The third comes from handwriting and tidiness. Good handwriting and tidy tables describe writing habits, not a type; remarks written like an essay do not mean a lack of rigour. Still less does any of this show who is better suited to quality work.

The fourth maps record content straight onto T/F: as though ISTJ records facts and INFP records feelings. Both can maintain a traceability chain, and both can consider what a record means for the people involved. T/F compares how much weight judgement gives to a consistent standard against human values — not who writes facts and who writes emotion.

body: In a fictional inspection meeting, either colleague might listen quietly or speak at length. Role, familiarity and the meeting format can all shape who speaks. Quietness does not tell you which person is more dependable.
At the letter level, both share Introversion. At the level of type dynamics, both stacks contain Fi, Ne, Si and Te. Neither similarity tells you whether the two people would look alike at work.

The difference runs along three preferences: in material, ISTJ more often trusts specific fact and experience, INFP more often trusts connection and possibility; in judgement, ISTJ more often gives the consistently applicable standard the main seat, INFP more often weighs people and values more heavily; in outer arrangement, ISTJ more often wants it settled, INFP more often wants to leave it open. The three axes have to be discussed separately — mixed together they become a personality verdict.
### INFP and ISTJ: the same inspection record, different attention

In a fictional quality review, three molded parts are sampled. Two are near the upper tolerance limit, and one is outside it. Both reviewers have the same measurements, gauge identifiers, procedure and reporting requirements.

Either reviewer must complete the required fields using the same procedure. When deciding how to explain the verified finding, both can weigh consistent reporting criteria and the risk of unfairly attributing responsibility. Those are possible T/F considerations. The order of filling in the form does not illustrate T/F or J/P.

Both emphases have a cost, and neither belongs to one type. Formatting alone can produce a complete record that cannot be read for the conditions at the time; writing the background at length can get the record returned on a mandatory field. How much that costs depends on who reads the record and what it is for.

In the fictional review, the report records the measured values, time and gauge identifier. The notes add that this was the first sample after a tooling change and that the next team was notified. The reviewer records the tooling change as a possible explanation that still needs verification.

The use of each kind of information needs stating. The traceability chain answers three things: who measured it, which revision of the procedure was used, and whether the downstream process was notified. It cannot establish that the anomaly came from the tooling change rather than equipment drift; verifying the cause means looking at equipment checks and process-parameter records, judged by whoever holds that responsibility. Neat handwriting and page count are not traceability evidence either — they are writing habits.
### INFP and ISTJ: why the four names match while the seating shifts two places

In the four-function notation used here, INFP is Fi–Ne–Si–Te and ISTJ is Si–Te–Fi–Ne. All four names are present and the order rotates by two seats: INFP's dominant Fi is third in ISTJ, and INFP's inferior Te is auxiliary in ISTJ; conversely, ISTJ's dominant Si is third in INFP, and ISTJ's inferior Ne is auxiliary in INFP.

The stacks share the judging pair Fi and Te and the perceiving pair Si and Ne. INFP leads with Fi, a judging process. ISTJ leads with Si, a perceiving process. The position in either stack says nothing about expertise or the order of steps in a real task.

Whether the third process is labelled introverted or extraverted is not uniform: for INFP's Si and ISTJ's Fi, some sources give an explicit attitude and others only the function name. When a different version turns up, check whether it names its source and read the pair through the first two positions; the disagreement does not change dominant and auxiliary. Base descriptions sit on the [INFP profile](/en/personality/infp) and the [ISTJ profile](/en/personality/istj).

body: The table assumes aligned conditions: the same moulded batch, the same record sheet, the same revision of the procedure, the same reviewer, the same mandatory requirements. If one is the inspector on shift and the other is only covering, duty will swamp both columns; if one has just had a record returned, behaviour will shift toward the stricter side too.

Both types can use both approaches below; the rows only state which kind of evidence tends to be taken first, and mark which axis each row sits on. This describes emphasis, not a scale of ability, and it must not be turned around into a typing table.

| The same situation | INFP: evidence likely to be attended to first | ISTJ: evidence likely to be attended to first | What this row illustrates |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A blank record sheet arrives | Keep several ways to organise the work open within the same required form | Agree on a provisional order for completing the same required fields | Outward stance, leaning J/P |
| Two parts near the upper bound, one out of tolerance | What patterns connect the measurements to the same documented process conditions | Measured values, gauge numbers and measuring times, each in its place | What counts as material, leaning S/N |
| The anomaly turns out to come from the previous process | Weigh how the required, verified details affect the people involved and make the context clear | Apply the same reporting criteria to the verified process and batch details | Standard of judgement, leaning T/F |
| The record sheet conflicts with the procedure | Within the approved reporting procedure, keep several ways to arrange the follow-up open | Within the same procedure, agree on a provisional follow-up schedule | Outward stance, leaning J/P |
| The record comes back marked "remarks too general" | How a reader will understand the situation from this line, and whether a team gets wrongly hurt | Which clause this line corresponds to, and whether it applies consistently to similar records | Standard of judgement, leaning T/F |
| Both review the same record three months later | Look for recurring patterns across this record and comparable batches, and list explanations that still need checking | Verify the batch, gauge, date and procedure revision against the original record | Information gathering: S/N |

None of these rows is a measure of proficiency. Someone who has inspected for ten years will usually fill every mandatory field out of professional habit whatever their type; someone filling the sheet independently for the first time may only try to say things clearly. The same person will also change approach with the information at hand, the duties of the shift and what the reviewer tends to look at, so these rows cannot be used to classify anyone.

body: Boundary of use: the three scenes below are fictional and involve only record keeping, communication and agreeing a division of work. They do not involve quality verdicts, equipment disposition or safety procedures. Anything touching a verdict or disposition follows company procedure and the person holding that responsibility.
A team can agree on what to document and how much context a later reader will need. Either colleague can spot a missing field or an incomplete explanation.
### INFP and ISTJ: before a factory audit, how the data chain and the explanatory page get split

(Fictional scene) A client is coming to audit and wants three months of records traced. The division follows who normally handles the records, who followed those two anomalies, and who knows the procedure revisions — not type. A common arrangement: whoever knows the logbooks builds the three months of sheets into one chain by batch and by procedure revision; whoever was on site writes a page explaining how the two anomalies were found, who was told and what changed afterwards.

Places missing a signature are marked and handled under the applicable records procedure. Where late signing is permitted, the actual signer, date and reason are kept — no back-dating, no signing for someone else; items that cannot be verified are left as they are rather than filled in to look tidy.

Two constraints apply. The explanatory page cannot replace the record: however detailed it is, a missing signature page is still a missing item. Nor can the chain replace the explanation: however complete, it cannot say why those two variations happened — the cause has to be verified separately.

In this fictional audit, the team samples three entries and checks who measured each part, which procedure applied and whether the next team was notified. This checks traceability in those entries. A qualified reviewer would investigate the causes separately using the relevant evidence.
### INFP and ISTJ: a cleaning rota in a shared flat

(Fictional scene) Two people share a flat and the living room and kitchen are never cleaned unless someone asks. One proposes a rota: who takes the rubbish out on which day, who mops at the weekend, tick when done. The other hesitates — will a rota turn the flatmate relationship into mutual assessment, with every missed turn recorded.

This is not about who is cleaner, and not a division by type. The one proposing worries that the work will always fall to the same person; the one hesitating worries that a table will fix things in writing and make living together harder later. Both concerns are legitimate.

A workable version splits the table into two columns: what must be done, and what gets done when noticed — only the first gets ticked. One counterexample: the proposer will also cover a flatmate's week during overtime without mentioning it, and the hesitant one will, after two weeks of putting up with it, stick the table on the fridge.

Agree a checkpoint: look at the table together on the last weekend of each month, adjust the division only, do not reopen old grievances. If someone genuinely stops doing their part over a long period, talk to them separately rather than reworking the whole table.
### INFP and ISTJ: the record comes back from review

(Fictional scene) The review comment comes back as "remarks too general". The first thing to do has nothing to do with type: establish whether the comment means the facts were unclear, that mandatory fields were missing, or both. Different targets, different fixes.

If the facts were unclear, what gets added is the process at the time: when it was discovered, which values it rested on, who was notified, how it was handled afterwards. If fields were missing, what gets added is the mandatory cells, units, signatures and dates. If both, list what is missing against the comment first, then decide what can be fixed on the spot and what needs verification back on site.

Responding to the same comment, the two may work differently: one more often compares clause by clause against the procedure to confirm the revised version passes the same requirements; the other more often restates the situation first to confirm that a reader will not misread where responsibility lies. Both work; who checks the revision afterwards follows duty, not type.

body: INFP does not indicate rule-breaking. A person of either type can know the procedure thoroughly and object to a record that omits facts or unfairly assigns blame.
ISTJ does not indicate indifference. A person of either type may insist on measured values because clear records protect coworkers as well as product quality.

The third comes from handwriting and tidiness. Good handwriting and tidy tables describe writing habits, not a type; remarks written like an essay do not mean a lack of rigour. Still less does any of this show who is better suited to quality work.

The fourth maps record content straight onto T/F: as though ISTJ records facts and INFP records feelings. Both can maintain a traceability chain, and both can consider what a record means for the people involved. T/F compares how much weight judgement gives to a consistent standard against human values — not who writes facts and who writes emotion.

body: When two results differ, check first whether it was the same item set, the same language version and the same scoring method, then look at the circumstances during that period: being in a position where your work is reviewed, a post whose requirements just changed, trouble at home — any of these can push self-description to one side. Worth noting down, but a single score cannot establish a stable tendency.

If the tool reports results for each preference dimension, look separately at the changes on S/N, T/F and J/P and at how close each sits to a boundary. This pair differs on all three, so explaining two results with two near-boundary axes is not enough, and neither of those two may be used to explain the third.

Put the practice where the procedure leaves room and the task conditions are comparable: pick a few records you filled recently and write three lines for each — what information you watched, what you based the judgement on, which arrangements you wanted settled early and which options you wanted kept open. What is written down is attention, not sequence; these notes serve only to understand your own preferences, are not used to assign a type and are not scored.

On the same record, either type may complete the formatting, and either may write the background at length; the difference is which kind of evidence gets leaned on more.
sections.title: Quick answer

sections.body_md:
In a fictional inspection meeting, either colleague might listen quietly or speak at length. Role, familiarity and the meeting format can all shape who speaks. Quietness does not tell you which person is more dependable.

At the letter level, both share Introversion. At the level of type dynamics, both stacks contain Fi, Ne, Si and Te. Neither similarity tells you whether the two people would look alike at work.

The difference runs along three preferences: in material, ISTJ more often trusts specific fact and experience, INFP more often trusts connection and possibility; in judgement, ISTJ more often gives the consistently applicable standard the main seat, INFP more often weighs people and values more heavily; in outer arrangement, ISTJ more often wants it settled, INFP more often wants to leave it open. The three axes have to be discussed separately — mixed together they become a personality verdict.

### INFP and ISTJ: the same inspection record, different attention

In a fictional quality review, three molded parts are sampled. Two are near the upper tolerance limit, and one is outside it. Both reviewers have the same measurements, gauge identifiers, procedure and reporting requirements.

Either reviewer must complete the required fields using the same procedure. When deciding how to explain the verified finding, both can weigh consistent reporting criteria and the risk of unfairly attributing responsibility. Those are possible T/F considerations. The order of filling in the form does not illustrate T/F or J/P.

Both emphases have a cost, and neither belongs to one type. Formatting alone can produce a complete record that cannot be read for the conditions at the time; writing the background at length can get the record returned on a mandatory field. How much that costs depends on who reads the record and what it is for.

In the fictional review, the report records the measured values, time and gauge identifier. The notes add that this was the first sample after a tooling change and that the next team was notified. The reviewer records the tooling change as a possible explanation that still needs verification.

The use of each kind of information needs stating. The traceability chain answers three things: who measured it, which revision of the procedure was used, and whether the downstream process was notified. It cannot establish that the anomaly came from the tooling change rather than equipment drift; verifying the cause means looking at equipment checks and process-parameter records, judged by whoever holds that responsibility. Neat handwriting and page count are not traceability evidence either — they are writing habits.

### INFP and ISTJ: why the four names match while the seating shifts two places

In the four-function notation used here, INFP is Fi–Ne–Si–Te and ISTJ is Si–Te–Fi–Ne. All four names are present and the order rotates by two seats: INFP's dominant Fi is third in ISTJ, and INFP's inferior Te is auxiliary in ISTJ; conversely, ISTJ's dominant Si is third in INFP, and ISTJ's inferior Ne is auxiliary in INFP.

The stacks share the judging pair Fi and Te and the perceiving pair Si and Ne. INFP leads with Fi, a judging process. ISTJ leads with Si, a perceiving process. The position in either stack says nothing about expertise or the order of steps in a real task.

Whether the third process is labelled introverted or extraverted is not uniform: for INFP's Si and ISTJ's Fi, some sources give an explicit attitude and others only the function name. When a different version turns up, check whether it names its source and read the pair through the first two positions; the disagreement does not change dominant and auxiliary. Base descriptions sit on the [INFP profile](/en/personality/infp) and the [ISTJ profile](/en/personality/istj).

sections.body_md:
The table assumes aligned conditions: the same moulded batch, the same record sheet, the same revision of the procedure, the same reviewer, the same mandatory requirements. If one is the inspector on shift and the other is only covering, duty will swamp both columns; if one has just had a record returned, behaviour will shift toward the stricter side too.

Both types can use both approaches below; the rows only state which kind of evidence tends to be taken first, and mark which axis each row sits on. This describes emphasis, not a scale of ability, and it must not be turned around into a typing table.

| The same situation | INFP: evidence likely to be attended to first | ISTJ: evidence likely to be attended to first | What this row illustrates |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A blank record sheet arrives | Keep several ways to organise the work open within the same required form | Agree on a provisional order for completing the same required fields | Outward stance, leaning J/P |
| Two parts near the upper bound, one out of tolerance | What patterns connect the measurements to the same documented process conditions | Measured values, gauge numbers and measuring times, each in its place | What counts as material, leaning S/N |
| The anomaly turns out to come from the previous process | Weigh how the required, verified details affect the people involved and make the context clear | Apply the same reporting criteria to the verified process and batch details | Standard of judgement, leaning T/F |
| The record sheet conflicts with the procedure | Within the approved reporting procedure, keep several ways to arrange the follow-up open | Within the same procedure, agree on a provisional follow-up schedule | Outward stance, leaning J/P |
| The record comes back marked "remarks too general" | How a reader will understand the situation from this line, and whether a team gets wrongly hurt | Which clause this line corresponds to, and whether it applies consistently to similar records | Standard of judgement, leaning T/F |
| Both review the same record three months later | Look for recurring patterns across this record and comparable batches, and list explanations that still need checking | Verify the batch, gauge, date and procedure revision against the original record | Information gathering: S/N |

None of these rows is a measure of proficiency. Someone who has inspected for ten years will usually fill every mandatory field out of professional habit whatever their type; someone filling the sheet independently for the first time may only try to say things clearly. The same person will also change approach with the information at hand, the duties of the shift and what the reviewer tends to look at, so these rows cannot be used to classify anyone.
sections.title: INFP and ISTJ in one minute

sections.body_md:
Boundary of use: the three scenes below are fictional and involve only record keeping, communication and agreeing a division of work. They do not involve quality verdicts, equipment disposition or safety procedures. Anything touching a verdict or disposition follows company procedure and the person holding that responsibility.

A team can agree on what to document and how much context a later reader will need. Either colleague can spot a missing field or an incomplete explanation.

### INFP and ISTJ: before a factory audit, how the data chain and the explanatory page get split

(Fictional scene) A client is coming to audit and wants three months of records traced. The division follows who normally handles the records, who followed those two anomalies, and who knows the procedure revisions — not type. A common arrangement: whoever knows the logbooks builds the three months of sheets into one chain by batch and by procedure revision; whoever was on site writes a page explaining how the two anomalies were found, who was told and what changed afterwards.

Places missing a signature are marked and handled under the applicable records procedure. Where late signing is permitted, the actual signer, date and reason are kept — no back-dating, no signing for someone else; items that cannot be verified are left as they are rather than filled in to look tidy.

Two constraints apply. The explanatory page cannot replace the record: however detailed it is, a missing signature page is still a missing item. Nor can the chain replace the explanation: however complete, it cannot say why those two variations happened — the cause has to be verified separately.

In this fictional audit, the team samples three entries and checks who measured each part, which procedure applied and whether the next team was notified. This checks traceability in those entries. A qualified reviewer would investigate the causes separately using the relevant evidence.

### INFP and ISTJ: a cleaning rota in a shared flat

(Fictional scene) Two people share a flat and the living room and kitchen are never cleaned unless someone asks. One proposes a rota: who takes the rubbish out on which day, who mops at the weekend, tick when done. The other hesitates — will a rota turn the flatmate relationship into mutual assessment, with every missed turn recorded.

This is not about who is cleaner, and not a division by type. The one proposing worries that the work will always fall to the same person; the one hesitating worries that a table will fix things in writing and make living together harder later. Both concerns are legitimate.

A workable version splits the table into two columns: what must be done, and what gets done when noticed — only the first gets ticked. One counterexample: the proposer will also cover a flatmate's week during overtime without mentioning it, and the hesitant one will, after two weeks of putting up with it, stick the table on the fridge.

Agree a checkpoint: look at the table together on the last weekend of each month, adjust the division only, do not reopen old grievances. If someone genuinely stops doing their part over a long period, talk to them separately rather than reworking the whole table.

### INFP and ISTJ: the record comes back from review

(Fictional scene) The review comment comes back as "remarks too general". The first thing to do has nothing to do with type: establish whether the comment means the facts were unclear, that mandatory fields were missing, or both. Different targets, different fixes.

If the facts were unclear, what gets added is the process at the time: when it was discovered, which values it rested on, who was notified, how it was handled afterwards. If fields were missing, what gets added is the mandatory cells, units, signatures and dates. If both, list what is missing against the comment first, then decide what can be fixed on the spot and what needs verification back on site.

Responding to the same comment, the two may work differently: one more often compares clause by clause against the procedure to confirm the revised version passes the same requirements; the other more often restates the situation first to confirm that a reader will not misread where responsibility lies. Both work; who checks the revision afterwards follows duty, not type.
sections.title: INFP and ISTJ at work and in relationships

sections.body_md:
INFP does not indicate rule-breaking. A person of either type can know the procedure thoroughly and object to a record that omits facts or unfairly assigns blame.

ISTJ does not indicate indifference. A person of either type may insist on measured values because clear records protect coworkers as well as product quality.

The third comes from handwriting and tidiness. Good handwriting and tidy tables describe writing habits, not a type; remarks written like an essay do not mean a lack of rigour. Still less does any of this show who is better suited to quality work.

The fourth maps record content straight onto T/F: as though ISTJ records facts and INFP records feelings. Both can maintain a traceability chain, and both can consider what a record means for the people involved. T/F compares how much weight judgement gives to a consistent standard against human values — not who writes facts and who writes emotion.
sections.title: INFP and ISTJ: avoiding misreads

sections.body_md:
When two results differ, check first whether it was the same item set, the same language version and the same scoring method, then look at the circumstances during that period: being in a position where your work is reviewed, a post whose requirements just changed, trouble at home — any of these can push self-description to one side. Worth noting down, but a single score cannot establish a stable tendency.

If the tool reports results for each preference dimension, look separately at the changes on S/N, T/F and J/P and at how close each sits to a boundary. This pair differs on all three, so explaining two results with two near-boundary axes is not enough, and neither of those two may be used to explain the third.

Put the practice where the procedure leaves room and the task conditions are comparable: pick a few records you filled recently and write three lines for each — what information you watched, what you based the judgement on, which arrangements you wanted settled early and which options you wanted kept open. What is written down is attention, not sequence; these notes serve only to understand your own preferences, are not used to assign a type and are not scored.
sections.title: INFP and ISTJ: how to keep observing

items.answer:
The pair shows how two types can share Introversion and the same four functions while differing on three preference pairs.

The resemblance ends there. The difference sits on S/N, T/F and J/P: material that trusts fact or connection, judgement that weighs a consistent standard or people and values, an outward face that settles an arrangement or keeps room. Quietness also depends on role, familiarity and the risk of conflict — either type can talk all through a meeting, and either can stay silent for the whole of one.
items.question: Both are introverted — why compare these two at all?

items.answer:
Fi and Si lead in different stacks under the convention used here. The function order does not predict how someone writes an inspection record. Both reviewers can meet the same documentation requirements and add verified context.

Position is not the order of actions. On the same sheet both may fill the data before writing the remarks, or the reverse; role, duty, experience, deadline and the amount of information available all rewrite the order. Telling the two apart means looking at which kind of evidence recurs across comparable situations, not at the order within one entry.
items.question: The four function names match — why do the records still read differently?

items.answer:
Sometimes yes, sometimes no — depending on duty, experience and the information available at the time, not on a type switch.

What can be confirmed is that adding background for a person does not conflict with writing responsibility by procedure. A line noting that the shift was running a new mould for the first time can sit beside the responsible process, the batch and the gauge, all present. An INFP does the same, and also writes only what the procedure asks. The difference is not who writes facts and who writes human concern, but how much weight judgement gives to a consistent standard and to people's circumstances.
items.question: Will an ISTJ speak up for someone in a record?

items.answer:
Not a question of type, but of who normally handles the records and who followed those two anomalies. Either type may produce a complete chain, and either may have only a pile of loose sheets.

An audit usually wants both: the chain answers who measured this and under which revision, the explanation answers how that variation was found, who was told and what changed. A chain alone invites the question of cause; an explanation alone invites the question of where the evidence is. The traceability chain proves only that records can be checked; the cause of an anomaly is read from equipment and process records.
items.question: An audit needs three months of traceability — what can each produce?

items.answer:
The rota and the bill-splitting sheet — any table that turns daily life into items.

The sticking point is not type but two legitimate concerns: one side fears the work always lands on the same person, the other fears a table turns the relationship into mutual scoring. A workable version splits into "must" and "when noticed", ticks only the first, reviews once a month adjusting only the division, and handles a persistent non-contributor in a separate conversation.
items.question: As flatmates, which table do they most often get stuck on?

items.answer:
First confirm whether both used the same tool, the same language version and the same scoring method; under different conditions, two results do not have to explain each other.

If the tool reports dimension scores, look at each: how much S/N, T/F and J/P moved, and how close each sits to a boundary. This pair differs on all three, so two near-boundary axes cannot settle the third. Post requirements or recent circumstances affect self-description, but whether a form happened to be on the desk, or how many times it had been filled, is no basis for assigning a type.
